paragraphs.title: The Prophet Awakens and Sees the Lampstand

answers: The angel who talked with him
easy.explanation: The angel that talked with the prophet came and awakened him from sleep.
easy.q: Who awakened the prophet at the beginning of the vision?

easy.explanation: The prophet saw a candlestick made entirely of gold.
easy.q: What did the prophet see in the vision?

easy.explanation: He saw two olive trees, one on each side of the bowl.
easy.q: How many olive trees did the prophet see?

answers: He asked the angel what they meant
medium.explanation: He asked, “What are these, my lord?”
medium.q: What did the prophet do after describing the candlestick and olive trees?

medium.explanation: The KJV says there was “a bowl upon the top of it.”
medium.q: What was upon the top of the candlestick?

answers: Because he did not know what it meant
Because he wanted to change the candlestick
Because the angel told him to build it
medium.explanation: When asked whether he knew what the things were, he answered, “No, my lord.”
medium.q: Why did the prophet ask the angel about the vision?

answers: It had a bowl, lamps, and pipes
It stood beside a great mountain
The prophet saw it after the house was finished
challenge.explanation: The vision includes a bowl, seven lamps, and seven pipes to the lamps.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the candlestick was a complex arrangement rather than a single object?

answers: He could not see the candlestick
challenge.explanation: His repeated questions show that he did not yet understand the meaning of the vision.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the prophet asking about the vision more than once?

answers: One was on the right and one on the left
challenge.explanation: One tree was on the right side of the bowl and the other on the left.
challenge.q: How were the two olive trees positioned in relation to the bowl?

paragraphs.title: Blessing Through God's Spirit and the Removal of Obstacles

easy.explanation: The message was given as the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel.
easy.q: To whom was the word of the LORD given?

easy.explanation: The LORD said, “Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit.”
easy.q: By what would the work be accomplished?

answers: It would become an olive tree
easy.explanation: The great mountain would become a plain before Zerubbabel.
easy.q: What would happen to the great mountain before Zerubbabel?

answers: The candlestick versus the olive trees
medium.explanation: The message contrasts might and power with the work of God's spirit.
medium.q: What is the main contrast in the LORD's message to Zerubbabel?

answers: A vessel for holding a lamp
medium.explanation: The mountain becoming a plain pictures an obstacle being made level.
medium.q: What is a plain in this passage?

medium.explanation: The verse says that he would bring forth the headstone with joyful cries.

answers: Obstacles would be removed through God's spirit
The mountain was part of the candlestick
challenge.explanation: The level plain represents the removal of the obstacle before Zerubbabel.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the mountain becoming a plain and the message to Zerubbabel?

answers: Joy and favor toward the stone and its work
challenge.explanation: The cry expresses rejoicing and favor as the headstone is brought forth.
challenge.q: What idea is expressed by the repeated cry “Grace, grace” concerning the headstone?

answers: The task before him involved a significant obstacle
He had no connection with the building
He was looking only at the candlestick
challenge.explanation: The great mountain represents a major obstacle in Zerubbabel's path.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the great mountain standing before Zerubbabel?

paragraphs.title: Completion of the House and the Day of Small Beginnings

easy.explanation: The passage says that Zerubbabel's hands laid the foundation and would finish the house.
easy.q: Who laid the foundation of the house and would also finish it?

easy.explanation: The KJV asks, “For who hath despised the day of small things?”
The people would see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel.

answers: The same Zerubbabel is connected with both stages
Only the angel is responsible for both stages
medium.explanation: The verse attributes both laying the foundation and finishing the house to Zerubbabel's hands.
medium.q: What connection is made between the foundation and the completion of the house?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a small or humble beginning that should not be despised.
medium.q: What does “the day of small things” mean in this context?

answers: Building work and its proper completion
medium.explanation: A plummet is a building tool, fitting the passage's emphasis on construction and completion.
medium.q: What does the plummet in Zerubbabel's hand represent?

answers: A humble beginning can lead to a completed work
There is no need to continue building
challenge.explanation: The passage encourages confidence that a small beginning can lead to completion.
challenge.q: What practical message comes from not despising the day of small things?

answers: They are the eyes of the LORD moving throughout the earth
They symbolize the number of houses
challenge.explanation: The verse identifies the seven as the eyes of the LORD, which run throughout the whole earth.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the seven eyes and God's oversight?

answers: Beginning the building, completing it, and watching over it
Awakening, sleeping, and leaving the candlestick
War, victory, and crowning a king
challenge.explanation: The passage includes the foundation, the completion of the house, and the LORD's watchful eyes.
challenge.q: Which combination of ideas appears in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Clarifying the Meaning of the Two Olive Trees

easy.explanation: He asked about the two olive trees and their branches beside the candlestick.
easy.q: What did the prophet continue to ask about?

answers: They emptied golden oil into the golden pipes
easy.explanation: The branches emptied golden oil through the two golden pipes.
easy.q: What did the two olive branches do?

answers: Zerubbabel and Joshua the high priest
easy.explanation: The two anointed ones are identified with the leaders Zerubbabel and Joshua.
easy.q: Who were the two anointed ones?

answers: They carried or received the golden oil
medium.explanation: The olive branches emptied golden oil through the two golden pipes.
medium.q: What were the two golden pipes used for in the vision?

answers: He still did not know what they meant
medium.explanation: His repeated question shows that he still needed the meaning explained.
medium.q: Why did the prophet ask about the olive trees again?

answers: They supplied oil through the branches and pipes
The candlestick changed into olive trees
medium.explanation: The branches supplied golden oil through the pipes connected with the lampstand.
medium.q: What connection did the olive trees have with the candlestick?

answers: The prophet already knew the answer
The trees were not part of the vision
challenge.explanation: The repeated questions and the prophet's answer, “No, my lord,” show that clarification was needed.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the angel explaining the olive trees only after repeated questions?

answers: They stand by the Lord of the whole earth
They move away from the house
challenge.explanation: The angel says they are the two anointed ones that stand by the LORD of the whole earth.
challenge.q: How are the two anointed ones described at the end of the passage?

answers: As the oil flows from the trees, the leaders stand in service before the LORD
The oil represents the leaders abandoning their work
The leaders are the golden pipes themselves
challenge.explanation: The vision shows oil flowing from the olive trees, while the interpretation identifies the trees with two anointed servants before the LORD.
challenge.q: What relationship is suggested between the oil and the two leaders?
